channel.title: Daily Perspective
channel.description: A daily digest of tech, world, economy and perspective.

item.title: Saturday, October 3, 2026
item.description: Behind each data-center protest, layoff statistic, and conflict headline is someone adapting with limited power. What would today's news look like if it centered their resourcefulness instead of just the systems acting upon them?

item.title: Friday, October 2, 2026
item.description: Behind every data center squeeze, jobs report, and conflict headline are people adjusting their lives in real time—whose daily reality today are you assuming too quickly you understand?

item.title: Thursday, October 1, 2026
item.description: Behind every policy debate—AI oversight, trade disputes, energy prices—are people absorbing the consequences. Whose daily life changes because of decisions made far from where they live?

item.title: Wednesday, September 30, 2026
item.description: Policies and products are designed at a distance from the people they affect—whose daily life would look different if you had to live inside the systems you build or approve?

item.title: Tuesday, September 29, 2026
item.description: Behind every efficiency metric—grid uptime, AI agents, facial recognition scans—there's a person unaccounted for. Whose burden are you not seeing in today's systems, and what would it take to notice them?

item.title: Monday, September 28, 2026
item.description: Behind every 'under-covered crisis' or 'labor market disruption' is someone's ordinary day upended. What would it take to let their reality reshape your sense of what's urgent?

item.title: Sunday, September 27, 2026
item.description: Behind every rate hike, safety pause, or 'AI interference' headline is someone recalculating their week—a family, a patient, a worker. What would today's news look like written from their vantage point instead of the system's?

item.title: Saturday, September 26, 2026
item.description: Somewhere today, someone is rationing gas to make tea while you decide what to have for lunch. Both are just people trying to hold onto something normal.
